### Method reminder

$|f(x)|<k$ (with $k>0$) is equivalent to $-k<f(x)<k$. Solve the double inequality, applying every operation to all three parts.

### Solution

$-5<2x-3<5$. Add 3 to every part: $-2<2x<8$. Divide by 2: $-1<x<4$.

Check: $x=0$ gives $|-3|=3<5$ (true) and $x=4$ gives $|5|=5$, not less than 5 (so the end points are excluded). The option $x<-1$ or $x>4$ is the solution of $|2x-3|>5$; $-2<x<8$ forgets to divide by 2.

### Method reminder

Factorise the quadratic to find its roots. For an upward parabola ($x^2$ coefficient positive), the quadratic is $\le 0$ between the roots and $\ge0$ outside them.

### Solution

$x^2-x-12=(x-4)(x+3)$, with roots $x=-3$ and $x=4$. The graph is an upward parabola, so it is below or on the $x$-axis between the roots. The inequality is not strict, so the roots are included:
$$-3\le x\le4.$$
The option $x\le-3$ or $x\ge4$ is the solution of $\ge0$; the other options come from using the wrong signs on the roots.

### Method reminder

Split by the sign of the expression inside the modulus, solve each case, then reject any solution that does not satisfy the condition of its own case (the right-hand side must also be $\ge0$).

### Solution

**Case $x\ge1$:** $x-1=3x-5\Rightarrow x=2$. Since $2\ge1$, it is valid (check: $|1|=1=3(2)-5$).

**Case $x<1$:** $-(x-1)=3x-5\Rightarrow1-x=3x-5\Rightarrow x=\tfrac32$. But $\tfrac32\not<1$, so this value is rejected (check: $|\tfrac12|=\tfrac12$ but $3\cdot\tfrac32-5=-\tfrac12$).

The only solution is $x=2$.

enonce_markdown: Find the set of values of $x$ for which $\dfrac{x+1}{x-2}\ge3$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Never multiply by an expression of unknown sign. Move all terms to one side, form one fraction, and study its sign with a table. Exclude values that make the denominator zero.

### Solution

$$\frac{x+1}{x-2}-3\ge0\Rightarrow\frac{x+1-3(x-2)}{x-2}\ge0\Rightarrow\frac{7-2x}{x-2}\ge0,\quad x\ne2.$$
Critical values: $x=2$ (excluded) and $x=\tfrac72$ (included, numerator zero).

| interval | $7-2x$ | $x-2$ | quotient |
|---|---|---|---|
| $x<2$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2<x<\tfrac72$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| $x>\tfrac72$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |

$$\boxed{2<x\le\tfrac72}$$
Check: $x=3$ gives $\tfrac41=4\ge3$ (true); $x=\tfrac72$ gives $\tfrac{9/2}{3/2}=3$ (true); $x=4$ gives $\tfrac52<3$ (false).

### Method reminder

When both sides are non-negative, $|a|>|b|\iff a^2>b^2$. Square both sides; the $x^2$ terms cancel and the inequality becomes linear.

### Solution

$(x+2)^2>(x-4)^2\Rightarrow x^2+4x+4>x^2-8x+16\Rightarrow12x>12\Rightarrow x>1.$

Geometric check: $|x+2|$ is the distance from $x$ to $-2$ and $|x-4|$ the distance to $4$; the midpoint of $-2$ and $4$ is $1$, and $x$ is farther from $-2$ than from $4$ when $x>1$. (Using $x>-1$ would come from averaging the wrong numbers.) Test: $x=2$ gives $4>2$ (true), $x=0$ gives $2>4$ (false).

### Method reminder

$|f(x)|<g(x)$ is equivalent to $-g(x)<f(x)<g(x)$ (which also forces $g(x)>0$). Solve each of the two inequalities separately and intersect the solution sets.

### Solution

$|x^2-4|<3x\iff-3x<x^2-4<3x$.

**Right part:** $x^2-3x-4<0\iff(x-4)(x+1)<0\iff-1<x<4$.

**Left part:** $x^2+3x-4>0\iff(x+4)(x-1)>0\iff x<-4\text{ or }x>1$.

Intersection of $-1<x<4$ with ($x<-4$ or $x>1$):
$$\boxed{1<x<4}$$
Check: $x=2$ gives $|0|=0<6$ (true); $x=5$ gives $21<15$ (false); $x=\tfrac12$ gives $\tfrac{15}{4}<\tfrac32$ (false).
